messages:
emma: FYI Polaris Compute reported failed marketplace install during node enrollment. Installer stage 2 exits with exit code 5 and the node never registers. They want the integration live before next Friday's joint announcement. Can we triage? @rafael can you take lead?

rafael: Put the logs here: https://files.redwood/polaris-install/logs-2026-03-20.txt

nio: Quick skim  seeing repeated `Failed to fetch artifact` and `401 Unauthorized` when hitting the artifact registry. Also lots of `dracut` errors during initramfs step: `could not find module: nvme_core`.

claire: Polaris uses image-based installs that expect NVMe drivers present. Their OEM image locks dm-crypt LUKS header with TPM binding. If installer can't unlock disk, services never start which explains the registration timeout.

rafael: Two problems then: 1) registry auth for model artifacts (401) and 2) missing kernel modules causing initramfs failure on their older firmware. Which do we want to tackle first?

emma: Registry auth is higher priority; marketing won't wait on firmware. Polaris says their proxy rewrites Authorization headers for long downloads which might break our presigned URL flow. Any suggestions to workaround?

partners-eng: We can provide a short-lived signed token flow that uses a POST to /artifact-proxy with a one-time token instead of presigned GETs. It's a small change on our side and Polaris can use it behind their proxy. Would require a 24h dev + a config toggle for their tenant.

nio: For the kernel modules: two options: ask Polaris to enable the `modprobe nvme_core` in their initramfs (requires rebuild) or provide an alternate installer image with the fallback path (detect NVMe absent and skip encryption-unlock step, then instruct ops to run manual disk setup). Rebuild will take time.

claire: Given timeline, recommend we: 1) patch registry auth (fast) 2) provide an interim installer shim that retries artifact download via the proxy and logs a clear actionable error for ops, 3) schedule firmware/initramfs remediation with Polaris engineering.

emma: Sounds good. Rafael, can you scope the auth patch and estimate? Also Polaris legal asked about joint announcement copy mentioning "supported on Polaris-certified nodes"  we should avoid committing to full compatibility until kernel/firmware is validated.

rafael: Auth patch estimate: 8 dev hours + 2 QA hours. We can ship a tenant-config toggle and a short runbook. I'll open a PR and a canary flag. Will need keys from Polaris to test the token exchange.

partners-eng: I'll draft a compatibility statement for marketing that says: "Supported on Polaris-certified hardware running validated firmware and kernel modules; contact Polaris for hardware qualification." Keeps us honest without blocking the announcement.

dev-bot: CI pipeline started for branch `polaris/auth-proxy` (build #824).

emma: Owners: rafael -> auth patch + PR, nio -> installer shim + clearer error codes, partners-eng -> marketing copy + test plan, claire -> firmware remediation plan with Polaris. Schedule a 30min sync tomorrow 09:00 PT.

polaris-ops@partners (via claire): We'll provide temporary test credentials and schedule a firmware maintenance window next week. We also need the exact token exchange spec to whitelist on our proxy.

rafael: Token exchange spec: POST /v1/tokens -> { tenant_id, node_id } returns { one_time_token, expires_at, artifact_url_post } ; artifact download flow: POST artifact_url_post with Authorization: Bearer one_time_token and body: { range, sha256 } -> returns stream. I'll email the full spec to Polaris.
